text: however. Other combinations that have also been tried include a corticosteroid with azathioprine, or a corti- costeroid with cyclophosphamide plus vincristine. Ciclosporin, alone or with a corticosteroid, has been used as a salvage therapy. Intravenous immunoglobulin has been tried, but any benefit is questionable. Similarly, plas- mapheresis and immunoadsorption have been used, but their contribution to the success of treatment is difficult to assess because they are usually combined with immuno- suppressive drug therapy. Factor VIII immune tolerance regimens are rarely, if ever, used in acquired haemophilia. 1. Bolton-Maggs PHB, Pasi KJ. Haemophilias A and B. Lancet 2003; 361: 1801–9. 2. World Health Organization.
